trigger: stop()/exception unwind while a genuinely in-flight parent-watch (P) read is outstanding
summary: p_dir's final RAII teardown (CancelIo+CloseHandle, no wait) does not drain a genuinely in-flight P read before the stack frame (p_buf/p_ov) is destroyed - a delayed kernel completion can write into reused/freed memory
classification_rationale: the file's own drain-pending machinery already treats this exact hazard as real for the mid-run reuse case, so treating final teardown as safe contradicted the codebase's own established handling of the same hazard class

trigger: every ordinary re-arm in file-exists mode (any qualifying content event on the guarded file)
summary: arm_watch_once() unconditionally closed X (the guarded file's directory) before blocking on P's full cancel-drain (up to 2x1000ms), on every ordinary re-arm - an availability regression on the primary detection channel, not a rare-race cost
classification_rationale: structural coupling of an unrelated secondary watch's teardown to the primary detection channel's availability, unconditional and on the security-detection reconcile path

trigger: an unrelated X-content event (or the hash-mode settle timeout) triggers arm_watch() while a real, unread P completion (a genuine rename detection) is already signalled
summary: p_reset() cancels and drains without ever calling GetOverlappedResult, discarding a real completion; the hash-mode timeout path (eval-then-arm ordering) is not self-healing and could leave the guard blocked indefinitely for that sequence
classification_rationale: the file's own header invariant (arm before presence-check, so a change in the gap re-fires) was violated at two call sites, making discard unsafe exactly where the invariant was relied on to make it safe

trigger: arm_parent_watch's P-open/read-failure path fires while X stays stable thereafter
summary: the P-open/read-failure path never set arm_retry, unlike every other watch-arm-failure path in the file; accidentally masked by P being retried as a side effect of ordinary X churn, which fixing UP-2 removes - would become a permanent, silent P disarm
classification_rationale: a required recovery scheduling step present on every sibling failure path was missing on this one
caused_by: the UP-2 fix removing P's incidental retry-on-churn side effect

trigger: a bad_alloc-class exception from fs::path/wstring construction after issue_p_read succeeds but before ownership transfers to pio
summary: bind()'s rebuild arm held fresh as a bare ParentIo* between new and ownership transfer into pio; a throw in that window (with a real overlapped read already pending) leaked both memory and OS handles silently, uncounted by kParentIoAbandonLimit
classification_rationale: new code using manual new/delete instead of RAII from the moment of allocation, the exact floor this file's own redesign exists to close for the analogous sec-1 case
adjudicated_by: cpp-safety (independently, same finding via a different argument)

trigger: a future maintainer reads the comment and 'fixes' the counter to reset-on-success
summary: p_abandon_count's comment claimed a 'consecutive' counter matching kParentFailureLimit's convention; the code is deliberately lifetime-cumulative (a driver stalling every other rebuild would never trip a reset-on-success cap) - code was correct, comment was a regression trap
classification_rationale: comment asserted behavior the code deliberately does not have

trigger: an operator reads the manual to judge whether FileGuard alone covers a rename of the watched directory's own parent
summary: the manual said a rename 'two or more levels above' the watched directory is undetected, implying the immediate parent's own rename IS detected live; verified false - P's own handle is opened with the same FILE_SHARE_DELETE semantics that make X's handle follow X's rename, so P's own rename is equally invisible - the boundary is one level, not two
classification_rationale: an I6 false-assurance escalation - the primary operator-facing document overclaimed real-time detection reach for a live security control

trigger: a future regression silently rebuilds P on every ordinary re-arm instead of retaining it
summary: run_retain_across_rearm asserted drift_count()==0 and eventual detection, neither of which can distinguish 'P was retained' from 'P was silently rebuilt every time' - a rebuild-every-time regression would still pass both checks
classification_rationale: the committed suite's only test for a previously-BLOCKING-severity property (UP-2) did not actually verify the distinguishing state

trigger: the guard's own compliance reporting path (report_compliant/eval_exists/eval_hash) after p_disabled becomes true
summary: p_disabled is never read by the compliance-reporting path; a rule whose rename-detection permanently died reports <compliant> identically to a fully healthy rule, with only a single log line as the ever signal - re-derived to MEDIUM (Fable) since GuardianEngine::get_status() already reports every rule unconditionally errored/unhealthy today, so there is no existing green signal for this to falsely contradict
classification_rationale: no per-guard health field exists yet for this or any other FileGuard degraded state; deferred to the already-named status-taxonomy follow-up rather than built in this diff
adjudicated_by: enterprise-architect (Fable): severity re-derived HIGH->MEDIUM, tracked-follow-up recommended over building a new status surface in this diff

trigger: a directory chain created one level at a time beneath a not-yet-existing watched path, or repeated independent unconfirmed drains over a rule's lifetime, on a lossy/degraded network share
summary: kParentIoAbandonLimit is lifetime-cumulative with no decay/window; arm_watch()'s own 3-attempt retry loop can compress '3 lifetime hits' into one ~6s episode if X's identity is flapping - severity assessed MEDIUM on local NTFS, HIGH/likely on SMB pending a real measurement; a rolling-window redesign was considered and rejected (Fable) as reopening the exact unbounded-leak the lifetime-cumulative design exists to prevent
classification_rationale: the manual did not yet document the concrete stepwise-directory-creation trigger mechanism, nor that it was measured rather than theorized
adjudicated_by: enterprise-architect (Fable): rolling-window redesign rejected on the file's own recorded leak-bound reasoning; deferred with reworded manual caveat naming the real trigger

trigger: the kParentIoAbandonLimit=3 cumulative-count to p_disabled=true transition
summary: run_parent_drain_forced_abandon forces and asserts exactly one abandon event (memory-safety/no-hang only); no test exercised the cumulative-count-to-disable transition itself, nor that bind() stops attempting rebuilds once disabled, nor that primary detection continues while P stays disabled
classification_rationale: the compliance-relevant behavior (permanent disable after 3) had no test coverage at all, only its single-event teardown precursor did

trigger: the operator's deferred disclosure decision, which depends on every residual being named somewhere durable
summary: 4 of 5 disclosure residuals (h_dir's identical teardown-drain gap, RegistryGuard's analogous no-parent-watch gap, the forced-dismount gap, the mount-point-change gap) existed only in this session's review-chain history, not durably in the repo; the governance ledger fragment for this branch was also empty at the time of this finding
classification_rationale: required disclosure-decision inputs were not captured anywhere a reviewer other than this session could retrieve them

trigger: this branch is ever pushed publicly
summary: two test commits itemize exact per-scenario red-before results (which specific cases fail, tripwire vs hash, filter strings, counts) - same specificity class flagged once already; recommends collapsing to aggregate pass/fail counts before any future push
classification_rationale: operator information/disclosure-hygiene nit on already-authored commit messages, not a code or doc defect
waiver_rationale: accepted as-is for this push: rewriting 28 commits' messages without -i history rewrite is disproportionate to the residual risk; left open for the operator to action separately if desired

trigger: the new abandon-chain test's TEST_CASE title claims the file's own detection is unaffected by P's disable
summary: the 5th assertion's comment attributed drift to X's own (h_dir) channel, but the wake was the ancestor watch (recursive, same mechanism as drifts #2-#4); h_dir was newly armed but never actually fired - the title's claim was asserted, not demonstrated
classification_rationale: a test comment and a TEST_CASE title both claimed a property the test did not exercise

trigger: a genuine (not test-forced) drain exceeds kCancelDrainMs on a loaded/contended CI runner
summary: hook_calls counts forced abandons only; a genuine drain timeout on a loaded runner would advance the real p_abandon_count without incrementing this counter, and would fail the CHECKs with a misleading signature (looks like a counting bug on otherwise-correct code)
classification_rationale: no comment distinguished a forced-vs-genuine abandon for a future flake triager

trigger: a reader of the manual's new empirical-measurement sentence infers that 100% sustained packet loss is 'the ordinary shape' of network degradation generally
summary: 'the ordinary shape of a degraded or congested WAN link, not a crash' generalized beyond the tested regime (only total/sustained loss was measured, not partial/intermittent loss); the operational conclusion itself was not false, only the typicality claim
classification_rationale: an unsupported generalization from a measured extreme case to a general characterization, distinct from the AV/EDR-interference overclaim explicitly checked for and not found

trigger: a reader of the manual's new sentence
summary: register leak ('private', 'measured, not merely theoretical' rather than the page's own established idiom), terminology drift across three near-synonym mentions of the same network condition in one paragraph, and an unhedged TCP-retransmission mechanism claim beyond what was directly observed (outcome-only measurement, not a packet-level diagnosis)
classification_rationale: wording register and internal terminology consistency, plus one mechanism claim routed as a truth question and resolved by hedging rather than asserting

trigger: agent shutdown or a GuardianEngine full_sync/rule-reconfigure teardown while N file-change guards on one device are all bound to a slow-cancel-confirming (e.g. lossy SMB) watched path
summary: stop_all_guards_locked() joins guards sequentially; each bound file-change guard's stop() now performs at least one bounded cancel-drain that did not exist pre-diff (h_dir's own teardown has no such wait) - N concurrently-armed guards on a slow-cancel path accumulate up to ~2N seconds of sequential shutdown latency, not evaluated against hard_exit.hpp's shutdown-grace budget
classification_rationale: no test or measurement exercises multiple concurrent FileGuard instances under this condition; named as a residual, not evaluated against the shutdown-grace budget in this diff
caused_by: the sec-1 fix adding a bounded drain wait to P's teardown, absent from X's own (h_dir) teardown
waiver_rationale: proportionate to defer: requires a multi-guard measurement rig and a hard_exit.hpp budget comparison beyond this diff's scope; named explicitly so it is not silently lost

trigger: CT-1-CT-2-CT-3-abandon-cap's open empirical question: does real network degradation on SMB actually exceed the 2x1000ms cancel-drain bound
summary: measured on a private, ephemeral SMB test rig (Docker/Samba, exercised from a real Windows client, fully torn down afterward): a frozen server (~95ms) and a fully severed connection (~289ms) both confirmed cancellation well under the bound; genuine mid-path packet loss (100%, container-scoped netem, no host-level change) reliably exceeded the 2000ms bound - settles the open question empirically rather than by inference, strengthening CT-1/CT-2/CT-3's severity beyond Fable's MEDIUM/possible re-derivation for the SMB case
classification_rationale: closes the measurement gap CT-1-CT-2-CT-3-abandon-cap left open; recorded here as its own finding since it changes the evidentiary basis (verified, not speculative) for that finding's severity
